browser.console_warnings: Eight repetitions of one Next.js CSS preload-not-used warning; no application exception or failed state transition.

scenario.step: Open the authenticated screenshot importer and select a local PNG
scenario.observed: The selected file remained in browser memory with editable crop and mask controls; no contact identity was requested before analysis.

scenario.step: Hold the screenshot-analysis response beyond the configured eight-second slow threshold
scenario.observed: A persistent status bar below the dialog title said the operation was taking longer than usual, remained safe to cancel, and had saved no source. Source-owner, replace, crop, and masking controls were disabled while the request was in flight.

scenario.step: Cancel the in-flight analysis on the 390-pixel responsive surface
scenario.observed: The request returned immediately to selection, announced that analysis was canceled and no source was saved, preserved the selected file, crop, and local masks, and re-enabled Read source for retry.

scenario.step: Compare account-scoped state before and after cancellation
scenario.observed: The People endpoint remained at 20 people and a summed capture count of 30 before and after cancellation. No person, source, or contact was created.

scenario.step: Repeat the slow and canceled states at 1440 by 1000
scenario.observed: The same truthful progress and recovery contract remained visible with zero browser console errors.

implementation_proof: The client owns one AbortController per analysis run, aborts on explicit cancellation, file replacement, dialog unmount, or a superseding run, and ignores stale completions.
The authenticated route passes request.signal through the screenshot-analysis abstraction to OpenRouter or Volcano Ark and returns an explicit no-store cancellation response when the caller aborts.
The server provider test aborts a caller signal and observes the combined provider signal abort with an AbortError.
The analysis endpoint has no persistence authority; reviewed persistence remains a separate explicit commit request.

kimi_webbridge.installer: Official installer completed and refreshed the binary and installed skills.
kimi_webbridge.reason: The daemon PID file points to macOS Passwords process 2158 while the HTTP status reports running=false; the Kimi skill prohibits stopping, restarting, or deleting that state automatically.

limits: The held browser response is a controlled degraded-network simulation; provider cancellation propagation is covered by the server test rather than a billable live-provider request.
VoiceOver, assistive-technology user testing, real-device background or relaunch, and offline launch remain unexecuted.
The browser uses synthetic evidence in an account-scoped local environment.
